course_name_original: Materiali e tecnologie per l'industria sostenibile
course_name_en: Materials and Technologies for Sustainable Industry
prerequisites: Industrial Engineering Materials course (module 1 and module 2) attended

Familiarity with basic concepts of general chemistry (atomic structure and chemical bonds, stoichiometry), organic chemistry (functional groups, molecular orbitals), and materials science (crystalline structures, diffusion and defects in crystals, phase diagrams, kinetics of phase transformations, mechanical properties and their characterization)

learning_outcomes.text: Acquisition of knowledge related to materials and technologies for sustainable industry, with particular reference to polymers, ceramics, metals, composites, in relation to use, life cycle assessment, and environmental impact.
Recognize and describe polymeric materials (thermoplastics, elastomers, and thermosets), their main properties, and polymerization and production technologies (traditional and innovative).
Distinguish and describe inorganic non-metallic solids with particular reference to glass, identify their properties, and related manufacturing processes.
Know and evaluate metallic materials and related technologies for sustainable industry (green steel; primary-secondary aluminum; net-shape technologies).
Classify and describe composite materials with their constituents (matrices, fillers, and reinforcements), and main production technologies; describe different types of carbon and their uses.
Classify the main additive manufacturing technologies; know and describe categories of materials-products (asphalt, wood, paper, cardboard).

Evaluate materials and technologies in view of applications and sustainability; consider packaging materials in view of recycling possibilities, and environmental aspects for a more sustainable industry.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the course. General information on materials, technologies and sustainability. Environment and sustainability. Notes on design criteria and life cycle. Recycling (metals, glass, plastics, rubbers, cellulose derivatives). Environmental contamination and regulations; SDGs in Agenda 2030; energy, water, CO2.

Polymeric materials. Classifications and recalls on structure/properties. Polymerizations of thermoplastics; cross-linking processes with TTT diagrams of thermosets and elastomers. Glass transition, crystallization and melting. Production technologies for elastomers (Banbury mixing and products).

Transformation technologies for thermoplastic materials (injection molding, extrusion, fibers and fabrics, thermoforming, blow molding, rotational molding). Foamed materials (production and application).

Inorganic and non-metallic materials: Raw materials for the ceramic, glass and cement industries; structure of silicates and model structures of ceramics; structure of glass; viscosity and relaxation; physical, chemical and optical properties of glass; mechanical properties and strengthening processes; production processes and glass recycling; carbon footprint of the glass industry.
Metallic materials for sustainable industry. "Green steel" or the production of steel with low environmental impact. Primary and secondary aluminum. Net-shape production technologies.
Composite materials. Classification, and recalls on structure/properties. Fillers and reinforcements. Carbon (diamond, graphite, carbon fibers, nanocarbons).
Production technologies and products in polymer matrix composites. Particular cases: asphalt; wood; cellulose and paper/cardboard.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (open questions and/or numerical exercises)

assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test containing open questions and/or numerical exercises. The precision and timeliness of the answers, the use of adequate technical-scientific language, and the correctness of the calculations performed will be evaluated. An optional mid-term test covering the first part of the course is also offered.
